title: Structural Opportunities, Agentic Practices, and Institutional Reproduction: The Mechanism of New Employment Groups’ Participation in Grassroots Governance—A Case Study of the “Rider Stations” in Beijing, China
content: Against the backdrop of the platform economy, transforming delivery riders and other new employment groups from objects of governance into forces of governance has become a critical issue in the modernization of grassroots governance. Existing studies focus either on structural domination or on one-dimensional empowerment, and thus struggle to explain the mechanism through which individual agency and macro-level institutions mutually constitute one another. This paper draws on structuration theory to construct an analytical framework of structural opportunity—agentic practice—institutional reproduction, based on qualitative data collected through participant observation and in-depth interviews. Find that riders face a fourfold structural dilemma of algorithmic domination, absent institutional channels, marginalized social identity, and scarce individual resources. The grassroots governance system creates actionable structural opportunities by providing rule-based channels, authoritative resources, symbolic resources, and platform resources. Riders proactively identify these opportunities through practical consciousness, convert their experiential capital into governance capital, accomplish the transition from practical consciousness to discursive consciousness and reflexive monitoring, and systematically construct self-identity, group identity, and social identity. The unintended consequences of their agentic practices, in turn, drive the institutionalization of governance positions, ultimately achieving institutional reproduction and a paradigm shift toward multi-stakeholder co-construction. These findings provide a theoretical foundation and practical insights for moving the governance of new employment groups from the empowerment of individual exemplars toward sustainable, collective ecosystem building.
